summary: 1. Key operational findings Oct 13 posted 22,475 BCM against a 24,072.2 BCM target (-6.63%), narrower than Oct 12's -7.15% miss. 2. MTD narrowed to 388,151 BCM against 421,263.8 (-7.86%), the second straight day of improvement (Oct 11 -7.98%, Oct 12 -7.93%, Oct 13 -7.86%), at day 19 of the 30-day fiscal cycle (11 days remaining). 3. Three things to flag: 1. 4. The waste/ore split reversed back toward normal after Oct 12's unusually ore-heavy day: waste missed by 10.97% (17,484 vs 19,637.3 BCM) while ore ran 12.54% over target (4,991 vs 4,435.0 BCM), pulling the day's stripping ratio back up to 3.50 from Oct 12's 1.63. 2. 5. The crusher logged its third straight zero-feed day (0 BCM, the planned shutdown that began Oct 11); MTD throughput sits at 9,753 LCM against a 78,533 LCM plan (12.42%, down from Oct 12's 13.11%), with no reopening date given yet. 3. 6. The excavator fleet partially recovered as EX-247 returned from Oct 12's full-day 1,000-hour service (down only 2 h today on hydraulic leakage and an engine warning), lifting daily excavator availability to 69.05% from Oct 12's 63.69%; on the dump-truck side DT-108's final-drive changeout and DT-346's unreconciled 24-hour "Daily Inspection" anomaly both cleared, but a new brake-air-pressure fault opened on DT-130 (22.5 h, 6.25% avail, no time-out logged by report cut-off). 7. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 69.05% day / 66.23% MTD; trucks 87.80% / 90.33%; drills 91.41% / 86.56%; overall 91.99% / 87.31%, core fleet 88.05% — the best overall daily reading since at least Oct 10. 8. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253, EX-263, EX-247) 16,440 BCM / 44,388 t gross; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-110, DT-130, DT-109) 5,128.4 BCM / 13,846.7 t — combined 21,568.4 BCM / 58,234.7 t, well above the day's 1,597.2 BCM target miss. 9. A Water Truck Tires email thread (Louw Weideman, 2026-10-14, 10:08 AM) asks procurement to source off-road-rated tyres for the water trucks, service truck, and fuel truck, citing repeated punctures — lands the same day WT-300 (second consecutive day on a tyre puncture, plus a fresh one overnight) and WT-304 (new tyre and brake air-pressure faults) both show tyre-related stoppages. Flag, not resolved: the Q4 recovery budget deck advanced to v29 (same scenarios as v28). A live email thread the same morning (Muneeb Ur Rehman, Joe Coleman, Ivan Anthony, Peter Anthony, 09:18-10:18 AM) disputes the deck's Slide 4 shortfall figure: Ma'aden's own letter states the contractor is behind target by approximately 500,000 tons, while the deck states a Jan-Sep shortfall of 1,310,877 t (-8.6%). Joe Coleman's reply argues the deck's 1.3 Mt figure is correct and agreed by both survey teams, suggesting Ma'aden's letter may have misread a 485,000 BCM figure as a tons figure — units, not magnitude, may be the actual discrepancy. No new survey file (261014-INX-SUM) has landed yet, so [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] was not updated this pass; its most recent reading remains Oct 12 production day (+742 BCM / +3.21% vs survey). The A&U, DPR, Drill Meters, Drill Sampling, Equipment Running Hours, Running Hours Maaden, and Grade Control Sheet workbooks gained Oct 13 tabs/edits but were registered by name only, not deep-read (the Client Meeting Report and the Daily Availability Final Report cover the figures compiled this pass). The October Distance Report was not updated this pass (no Oct 13 tab yet). The Q4 recovery deck v29 and its superseded _archive versions were registered by name only beyond the first six slides read. `publish_insights.py` was deliberately not run this pass — the `wiki-insights-sync` task publishes separately at 11:00/17:00. Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
